findings.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant check is inverted and mis-offset: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the matcher when the shortcut MATCHES and passes it when it doesn't, and substring(3,5) reads tokenType's 2nd char + grant's 1st char instead of the grant shortcut at indices 4-6. The grant assertion the diff adds to expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken is vacuous: any encoded token id passes regardless of which grant shortcut was embedded (e.g. 'onrtcc:uuid' passes an expectation of 'dg'), so a regression that encodes the wrong grant type into token ids and event TOKEN_ID details cannot be caught by these tests; the comment ('starts at 4th char') is also wrong (grant starts at 5th char).

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never null-checks rawTokenId, so the second check is dead code and a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. A null rawTokenId passes construction and later surfaces as a token id of 'xxyyzz:null' or an NPE at encode/decode time far from the actual bug site, instead of the intended fail-fast; the field invariant the class documents is not enforced.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason: the test never calls factory.postInit, so `sessionFactory` is null and getGrantTypeByShortcut('ac') throws a NullPointerException from `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which is swallowed by the broad `catch (RuntimeException iae)`. The test would still pass if the production code stopped throwing IllegalArgumentException for unknown grant shortcuts and instead crashed or returned null — it verifies only 'some RuntimeException happens', masking real behavior changes in the decode path.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the logic that decides SessionType (online/offline/transient), TokenType (lightweight via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken), and the GRANT_TYPE-attribute-to-'na' fallback — has no test coverage in this diff; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only exercises encode/decode of the id string. A regression in session-type detection (e.g. offline tokens encoded as 'on') or in the lightweight-token branch would mint systematically mis-tagged token ids that later decode to the wrong context, and no test in this change would fail.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps' paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut write into the shortcut maps at runtime without the duplicate-shortcut validation performed in postInit, and only scan currently-registered factories, so feature-gated grants (CibaGrantTypeFactory and DeviceGrantTypeFactory implement EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory) are absent from the maps whenever their profile feature is off. If a colliding shortcut is introduced via the lazy path it silently evicts the existing grant's mapping and previously issued token ids decode to the wrong grant type; conversely, disabling CIBA/OID4VC_VCI or the device profile after tokens were issued makes getTokenContextFromTokenId throw IllegalArgumentException ('Unknown value ... for grant type') for those already-minted ids.

[ADVISORY] initToken changes the access token id (jti and event Details.TOKEN_ID) from a plain UUID to the 'xxyyzz:uuid' encoded format, but only four AssertEvents matchers are updated — every other consumer that assumes the id is a UUID is silently left behind. Any test or out-of-tree tooling that parses Details.TOKEN_ID / the jti claim with UUID.fromString or matches it with isUUID() (patterns used throughout the testsuite and by external integrations reading Keycloak events) breaks or silently mismatches once tokens minted by this code path are observed; the diff updates only the matchers its author knew about.

[ADVISORY] getShouldUseLightweightToken is widened from a package-private instance method to a public static method on AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper so the encoder can call it, promoting a mapper-internal decision into de-facto public API on a class that third-party protocol mappers extend. Once released, external protocol-mapper implementations can couple to this static, and the 'should use lightweight token' policy now lives in the mapper class while its consumers live in the encoder package — the next change to the policy (e.g. moving it to a client-policy or realm attribute) has to chase callers across both surfaces instead of one.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher's grant check is doubly broken: it reads items[0].substring(3, 5) (off-by-one — the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix) and its logic is inverted (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects a match instead of requiring one), and because the tokenType shortcut's second char is always 't', substring(3,5) is always "t"+grant[0], which never equals any registered shortcut — so the equals branch is dead code and the matcher accepts ANY grant shortcut. Every integration test using expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken now verifies only that TOKEN_ID has two colon-separated segments with a UUID tail; a regression that encodes the wrong grant shortcut (or no shortcut at all) into access token IDs passes CI — the PR's core acceptance criterion (grant type is correctly encoded into the token ID and observable in events) is silently unverified despite the tests appearing to assert it.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed") twice; the second call was clearly meant to validate rawTokenId (its message even says "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so a null rawTokenId passes validation. A null rawTokenId flows into encodeTokenId and produces a token ID of the form "onrtcc:null" (or NPEs downstream in decode's substring logic) instead of failing fast at construction with the intended diagnostic.

[ADVISORY] The only test added for this feature never exercises getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (sessionType derivation from persistence state and isOffline(), lightweight-token detection, the null-GRANT_TYPE fallback to "na") nor the factory's postInit wiring (real shortcut registration from grant providers and the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException); all five tests hand-build the shortcut maps and only round-trip decode/encode of literal strings. The half of the encoder that actually derives context from a live client session — the code with the most branching and the highest regression risk (e.g., isOffline vs TRANSIENT precedence, lightweight detection via session context client) — has zero coverage; a regression there ships unnoticed, and the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation that protects against a new grant colliding with an existing shortcut is likewise untested (verified: the diff contains exactly one test file for this feature and it contains no such assertions).

[ADVISORY] initToken switches every newly issued access token's jti from a UUID to the "xxXXxx:uuid" encoded format unconditionally and with no configuration gate, yet no production code in this diff consumes getTokenContextFromTokenId — and no acceptance criterion or compatibility note addresses the globally changed token-ID surface. The encode half of the framework is live on day one (all access token IDs in events, logs, admin APIs, and any external system that parses jti as a UUID change format immediately) while the decode half has no caller, so the format change carries all of its compatibility risk with none of its benefit until a future PR wires the consumer; out-of-tree tooling or integrations assuming UUID jti break without any flag to revert.

[ADVISORY] GRANT_TYPE attribution is set only on the token-endpoint grant paths (createTokenResponse, ROPC, pre-authorized code, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, refresh validateToken), but other token-issuing paths that also reach initToken — implicit/hybrid authorization-endpoint flows and the legacy AbstractTokenExchangeProvider exchange path (the parent whose exchangeClientToOIDCClient StandardTokenExchangeProvider overrides) — set no GRANT_TYPE attribute. Tokens from those paths silently encode grant shortcut "na" while the same encoder reports real shortcuts for every other flow, so the encoded context is inconsistent across the token-exchange family and meaningless for implicit-flow tokens; any existing test asserting Details.TOKEN_ID via isUUID() on those flows (not among the four expect* helpers updated here) fails once the encoded format lands, and the "grant type used" contract the Constant documents is silently not honored for those paths.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId checks the wrong character range and inverts the equality test: it does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` while the encoded prefix is st(0-1)+tt(2-3)+grant(4-5), so the grant shortcut lives at substring(4,6) and a match should cause acceptance, not rejection. The matcher accepts any 6-char prefix regardless of grant (e.g. 'onrtna:uuid' passes expectCodeToToken which expects 'ac'), so all four updated event assertions (code, device, refresh, CIBA) verify nothing about grant encoding; and if the checked range ever does equal the expected shortcut the test fails spuriously. The grant encoding could regress to 'na' for every grant and CI stays green.

[BUG] The diff wires encoding into the global hot path (every access token ID becomes 'onrtac:<uuid>' instead of a UUID via encoder.encodeTokenId) but no production code anywhere in this diff ever calls getTokenContextFromTokenId, so the decode half of the framework is dead code and the only reachable production effect is the token ID format change itself. Every consumer that assumes access token IDs are UUIDs (Details.TOKEN_ID event consumers and external integrations, as evidenced by the forced isUUID() removals in AssertEvents) breaks now, while the feature that justifies the format change delivers zero behavior in this PR; the framework ships with an unexercised decode path that will only get its first real consumer in some future diff.

[ADVISORY] The Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted as untraceable drive-by cleanup rather than updated to copy the new grantType field, silently removing a public constructor from the server-spi-private surface. Out-of-tree custom grant providers that call new Context(context) fail to compile against this version with no deprecation cycle; and if the constructor is later re-added to fix that, the author must remember to also add the grantType copy, which is exactly the field the deleted version predates.

[ADVISORY] grantType is snapshotted from formParams only in the constructor while setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap) can replace formParams afterwards without updating grantType, leaving two mutable fields in the same object that can silently disagree. Any caller that uses setFormParams after construction (the method exists precisely for that) gets a Context whose getGrantType() no longer matches getFormParams(), and the wrong grant shortcut is then encoded into the token ID with no error; the next change that routes form-parameter rewriting through setFormParams inherits this divergence.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only production-facing mapping logic in the new provider (transient/offline/online detection, lightweight-token detection, grant attribute fallback to UNKNOWN) — has no test in this diff, and the DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest round-trips hand-built shortcut maps instead of the real postInit registry. A regression in sessionType or lightweight detection, or a grant flow that never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, encodes wrong context into every issued token ID silently; the per-grant propagation added in OAuth2GrantTypeBase, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType and StandardTokenExchangeProvider is verified nowhere because the AssertEvents matcher (see separate finding) accepts any grant shortcut.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant check is doubly broken: `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts the wrong two characters (the grant shortcut lives at indices 4-5 in the 2+2+2 layout, not 3-4), and the guard `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` inverts the logic, rejecting the ID when the grant MATCHES. The matcher accepts any grant shortcut whatsoever (substring(3,5) can never equal a valid shortcut like "ac" or "rt" for a well-formed encoding, and even if it did, equality returns failure). Every assertion built on expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken passes vacuously regardless of which grant the token was issued under, so a regression that stamps the wrong grant shortcut into token IDs ships green.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") twice — the second check re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is never rejected. A null rawTokenId flows into encodeTokenId, where string concatenation renders it as the literal 'null' suffix ('onrtac:null'), producing tokens whose raw id is the constant string 'null' instead of failing fast at construction; the misleading message also misdirects whoever debugs the eventual NPE-free corruption.

[ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts without validating that each is exactly 2 characters and free of ':', so a factory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut produces encoded token IDs whose context prefix length is not 6. The server mints access tokens (initToken -> encodeTokenId) that its own decoder then rejects forever: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on the `encodedContext.length() != 6` check, so every downstream consumer of such a token ID (the whole point of the encoder) fails. OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an extension point, so this is not hypothetical.

[BUG] The lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut put() into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts unconditionally with no collision check, bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs. When a new grant implementation is later deployed (the exact scenario the refresh path exists for) and its shortcut collides with an existing one, the put silently overwrites the mapping and previously issued tokens carrying that shortcut decode to the wrong grant type; the size-equality guard that protects the startup path protects nothing here.

[ADVISORY] Encode and decode degrade asymmetrically: encode lazily learns unknown grants (or falls back to 'na' for null), but getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on any unknown session/token/grant shortcut rather than mapping it to UNKNOWN. During a rolling deploy where a new grant type (or a new shortcut) exists on some nodes but not others, or after a grant provider is removed, the nodes lacking the registration throw a hard error on token IDs their peers issued, instead of degrading to SessionType.UNKNOWN/TokenType.UNKNOWN the way the legacy no-colon path already does — turning a partial deployment into user-visible token-processing failures.

[ADVISORY] The token-ID layout (2-char sessionType + 2-char tokenType + 2-char grant + ':' + uuid) is now hand-maintained in three places — the encoder's concatenation, the decoder's substring offsets, and this matcher — and the copies have already drifted (matcher uses substring(3,5) and a wrong comment about the '4th char'). The next change to the encoded format (adding a field, resizing a segment) must be applied in three independent sites across two modules; the drift that already happened here shows the pattern fails silently, and the next copy will again compile and pass while disagreeing with the encoder.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted outright rather than updated to carry the new grantType field, removing a public constructor from a server-spi-private class that custom grant implementations may call. Any extension or out-of-tree caller that copied a Context (the constructor existed precisely to support deriving a context from an existing one) fails to compile against this version, and there is no in-diff replacement that preserves the copy-with-grantType behavior it would now need.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher inverts its grant-type check and reads the wrong substring: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` both indexes characters 3-4 (token-type tail + grant-type head) instead of the grant shortcut at characters 4-5, and returns false (mismatch) when they DO match. Because no real grant shortcut can occupy characters 3-4 of the 6-char prefix (position 3 is always 't' for token types 'rt'/'lt', and no shortcut starts with 't'), the equals branch never fires and the matcher degenerates to only checking that the suffix is a UUID — the PR's test harness silently stops verifying grant-type encoding entirely, so a regression in grant encoding passes the suite. Conversely, if a grant shortcut starting with 't' is ever added, valid tokens start failing this matcher with a confusing mismatch.

[BUG] The constructor contains a copy-paste duplicate null-check — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId passes construction and flows into encodeTokenId, producing token IDs like 'onrtac:null' that later fail UUID validation and correlate every such token to the same literal id; the guard the message promises does not exist.

[ADVISORY] All access-token jti values silently flip from UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' unconditionally in initToken, with no feature flag, realm option, or provider default that restores the legacy format (only the fallback decoder tolerates old IDs; there is no off switch for new issuance). Every external consumer and operator tooling that assumed the UUID jti format — an invariant the test suite itself encoded in isUUID() until this PR — starts seeing the new composite format on upgrade with no way to opt out short of deploying a different SPI provider; this format change to a publicly observable token field goes well beyond 'implement the framework' and should be an explicitly accepted decision, not a side effect of wiring the default encoder.

[ADVISORY] The unit test bypasses the factory's real wiring by hand-populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts in before(), so postInit registration, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation, and both lazy-refresh fallbacks in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory have zero coverage. A regression in the registry — e.g., the startup duplicate-shortcut check firing on the stock grant set, a lazy refresh writing a colliding shortcut over an existing mapping (the runtime put calls bypass the size-based validation entirely), or getShortcutByGrantType returning the wrong grant — ships unnoticed, while the tests that do exist only exercise a two-grant hand-built map.

[ADVISORY] The constructor's null-check for rawTokenId is a copy-paste error: it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time, so the documented 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' invariant is never enforced. A caller that passes a null rawTokenId bypasses the fail-fast contract and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId silently produces a structurally valid but garbage token id ending in ':null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null'), which then flows into the issued access token's jti and event logs; the guard that was written to catch this exact case is dead code because the wrong variable is checked.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException (not an error signal distinguishable from a crash) for any client-influenced token-id string that contains a colon but has an invalid 6-char prefix or unknown shortcut, rather than degrading to the UNKNOWN/old-format handling used for colon-less ids. The new public provider API is explicitly intended for decoding token ids retrieved from tokens; any current or future call site that passes an untrusted token-id string (introspection/revocation token hints, event-detail lookups, stored session references) without try/catch turns malformed user input into an unhandled RuntimeException and an HTTP 500 on the endpoint, instead of the old-format fallback path the same method defines two branches earlier; the exception messages also echo the raw attacker-controlled string back into server logs/error handlers.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher's grant-shortcut check is doubly broken (inverted condition plus wrong substring offset), so it can never fail on grant content and the matcher degenerates to a bare 'colon followed by UUID' check. Line 483 reads `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` — two independent bugs: (1) the condition returns false (mismatch) when the shortcut EQUALS the expected value, the inverse of the intent; (2) substring(3,5) extracts chars 3-4, which are the tokenType shortcut's 2nd char plus the grantType shortcut's 1st char (grant shortcut actually lives at indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, contradicting even the comment on line 482). Since tokenType shortcuts are 'rt'/'lt'/'un', substring(3,5) is always 't?' or 'n?', which never equals any registered shortcut ('ac','cc','rt','ci','dg','pg','pc','te','ro','na'), so the guard never fires and matchesSafely reduces to `items.length == 2 && isUUID().matches(items[1])`. Every integration test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore passes even if TokenManager.initToken encodes no grant type, the wrong grant type, or a garbage prefix — the entire purpose of switching these expectations from isUUID() to isAccessTokenId(shortcut) is unverified, giving false confidence that the new context-encoding wiring works end-to-end.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes vacuously via a NullPointerException from the uninitialized factory, not via the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' validation, and the broad catch(RuntimeException) guarantees any exception satisfies it. The @Before method (lines 33-44) never calls factory.postInit(), so factory.sessionFactory stays null and grantsByShortcuts contains only 'ro','cc','na'. getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678") resolves shortcut 'ac' via factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which finds nothing in the map and dereferences the null sessionFactory in its lazy-refresh path (`sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory), throwing NullPointerException — which the catch (RuntimeException iae) on line 76 swallows, so the test passes. The IllegalArgumentException('Unknown value ... for grant type') path the test name claims to verify is never reached; the test would equally pass on a StringIndexOutOfBounds or any other crash, and even after fixing the NPE, catch(RuntimeException) instead of IllegalArgumentException with a message assertion means the test still cannot distinguish the intended validation error from an unrelated failure.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only encoder path actually used in production (TokenManager.initToken) — nor the factory's postInit registration/duplicate-shortcut validation or lazy-refresh logic. Test files checked: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java (the only test file in this diff touching the encode package) — all five tests drive getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId round-trips against hand-built maps; none call getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, so the sessionType derivation (TRANSIENT vs isOffline vs ONLINE), the lightweight-token detection via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, and the Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute-to-'na' fallback are completely unverified — a regression there (e.g. misclassifying offline sessions or picking the wrong session from clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()) ships green. Additionally, before() hand-assigns grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts instead of calling postInit, leaving the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit) and both lazy-refresh branches (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut with a live sessionFactory — the rolling-deploy path for newly deployed grants) untested; the NPE in testIncorrectGrantType is direct evidence that the refresh path behaves differently from what the tests assume.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' guard never runs. A null rawTokenId passes construction silently and encodeTokenId then produces a token ID with the literal suffix ':null', which later fails the 6-char-prefix decode check in getTokenContextFromTokenId and cannot be round-tripped; the intended fail-fast invariant (all four fields non-null) does not hold.

[ADVISORY] The lazy-map-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut write new grant/shortcut pairs into the maps with plain put() and no duplicate-shortcut validation, bypassing the size-equality check that postInit performs. When a new grant provider is registered after postInit and its getShortcut() collides with an existing grant's shortcut, the put() silently overwrites the existing mapping, so tokens already minted with that shortcut decode to the wrong grant type — a silent repurposing of an existing encoded value with no startup-time error to catch it.

[ADVISORY] grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are non-final, package-private mutable maps initialized only in postInit, with lookups reading them lazily afterwards. Any lookup (encodeTokenId or getShortcutByGrantType) invoked before postInit completes dereferences null and throws NPE, and the mutable package-visible state is a second initialization path (the new unit test already bypasses init/postInit and assigns the maps directly), so the next change that touches factory lifecycle risks an uninitialized-maps failure that startup validation will not catch.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second call, intended to validate rawTokenId, re-checks grantType, so a null rawTokenId passes validation. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and flows into encodeTokenId, producing token jti values like 'onrtcc:null'; the fail-fast guard promised by the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' message never fires, and the misleading message blames grantType when debugging.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) (the tokenType's last char plus the grantType's first char) instead of substring(4, 6), AND inverts the match condition — 'if (equals(expected)) return false' — so the grant assertion can never fail for a wrong grant and would fail for the correct one. Every event assertion using this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) silently passes regardless of which grant type was encoded into the token ID; the matcher only checks '6-char prefix : UUID', so a regression encoding the wrong grant into token IDs ships undetected — the assertion reports verification success while verifying nothing.

[ADVISORY] postInit validates shortcut uniqueness by map-size comparison but never validates that each grant shortcut is exactly 2 characters, while the getShortcut() javadoc in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory actively recommends '3-letters shortcut'. A grant factory (especially a custom one following the javadoc) returning a 1- or 3-char shortcut passes startup validation, but every token it produces gets a 5- or 7-char prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with 'Expected length of 6' — all tokens for that grant fail any future decode, and the misdocumented contract steers implementers into exactly that breakage.

[ADVISORY] The lazy re-registration branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut (commented 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed') are unreachable in practice because postInit already registers every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory at boot, and if they ever do execute they add mappings via ConcurrentHashMap.put without the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit enforces. Dead code that carries a correctness hazard: if any runtime path ever registers a grant factory after postInit, a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing grantsByShortcuts entry, so previously issued tokens decode as the wrong grant type with no error — the exact corruption the postInit check exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws raw IllegalArgumentException on attacker-craftable jti content (wrong 6-char prefix length, or unknown session/token/grant shortcut) and no caller in this diff catches it. The jti of an access token is client-visible and client-controllable in crafted tokens; any future caller that invokes this method during token validation, introspection, or logout converts a crafted jti into an unhandled RuntimeException and a 500 response where an invalid-token 4xx belongs. No shipped path in this diff is affected yet, but the provider contract invites exactly that caller.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor Context(Context context) is deleted from the Context class with no replacement, removing part of the public surface of server-spi-private. Out-of-tree code (custom grant implementations or wrappers around the grant SPI) that relied on copying a Context no longer compiles or fails to link after upgrade; nothing in the diff signals this removal to extension authors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher's grant check is doubly broken: it reads items[0].substring(3, 5) (off-by-one — the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix) and its logic is inverted (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects a match instead of requiring one), and because the tokenType shortcut's second char is always 't', substring(3,5) is always "t"+grant[0], which never equals any registered shortcut — so the equals branch is dead code and the matcher accepts ANY grant shortcut. Every integration test using expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken now verifies only that TOKEN_ID has two colon-separated segments with a UUID tail; a regression that encodes the wrong grant shortcut (or no shortcut at all) into access token IDs passes CI — the PR's core acceptance criterion (grant type is correctly encoded into the token ID and observable in events) is silently unverified despite the tests appearing to assert it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GRANT_TYPE attribution is set only on the token-endpoint grant paths (createTokenResponse, ROPC, pre-authorized code, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, refresh validateToken), but other token-issuing paths that also reach initToken — implicit/hybrid authorization-endpoint flows and the legacy AbstractTokenExchangeProvider exchange path (the parent whose exchangeClientToOIDCClient StandardTokenExchangeProvider overrides) — set no GRANT_TYPE attribute. adjudication.rationale: The diff makes access token IDs always encoded with context in `TokenManager.initToken()` via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`, and that provider reads `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` from the `ClientSessionContext`, defaulting to `UNKNOWN`/"na" when absent (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`, `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`). However, because those other flows are not shown in the diff, the claim about specific missing paths and failing tests cannot be fully verified here, and the implementation explicitly tolerates unknown grant type, so it’s more of a completeness/consistency concern than a definite broken behavior proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId checks the wrong character range and inverts the equality test: it does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` while the encoded prefix is st(0-1)+tt(2-3)+grant(4-5), so the grant shortcut lives at substring(4,6) and a match should cause acceptance, not rejection. adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the matcher logic is incorrect: it extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when it equals expectedGrantShortcut. Given the new token-id encoding elsewhere in the diff uses a 6-char prefix (sessionType 2 + tokenType 2 + grantType 2) before ':', the grant shortcut should be at substring(4, 6) (0-based). As written, the matcher will (a) not actually assert the expected grant shortcut (it accepts any prefix as long as the raw part is a UUID) and (b) spuriously fail if the wrong slice happens to equal the expected shortcut. This is a verifiable defect in the updated tests introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant check is doubly broken: `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts the wrong two characters (the grant shortcut lives at indices 4-5 in the 2+2+2 layout, not 3-4), and the guard `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` inverts the logic, rejecting the ID when the grant MATCHES. The matcher accepts any grant shortcut whatsoever (substring(3,5) can never equal a valid shortcut like "ac" or "rt" for a well-formed encoding, and even if it did, equality returns failure). Every assertion built on expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken passes vacuously regardless of which grant the token was issued under, so a regression that stamps the wrong grant shortcut into token IDs ships green.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded prefix layout is 2(sessionType)+2(tokenType)+2(grant)+':'+uuid, as implemented by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId (concatenates 6 chars then ':'). Therefore the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which extracts chars 3-4 (e.g., for "onrtac" it yields "ta"), so it will not match the expected grant. Additionally, the condition `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted (it rejects when it matches instead of when it doesn't). Together this makes the matcher effectively only validate the UUID part and not the grant shortcut, so the related event assertions can pass without verifying the intended grant encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") twice — the second check re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is never rejected. A null rawTokenId flows into encodeTokenId, where string concatenation renders it as the literal 'null' suffix ('onrtac:null'), producing tokens whose raw id is the constant string 'null' instead of failing fast at construction; the misleading message also misdirects whoever debugs the eventual NPE-free corruption.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (so `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected). This is verifiable in the added file `AccessTokenContext.java`. If a null `rawTokenId` is ever passed (e.g., via `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(..., rawTokenId)`), `encodeTokenId` will concatenate it (`':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`), yielding an encoded token id ending with the literal `"null"` rather than failing fast, and the exception message is misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts without validating that each is exactly 2 characters and free of ':', so a factory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut produces encoded token IDs whose context prefix length is not 6. The server mints access tokens (initToken -> encodeTokenId) that its own decoder then rejects forever: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on the `encodedContext.length() != 6` check, so every downstream consumer of such a token ID (the whole point of the encoder) fails. OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an extension point, so this is not hypothetical.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SPI method `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` (with Javadoc saying it is “usually like 3-letters shortcut”) and then encodes token IDs as `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut + ':' + rawId` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()`. However, the decoder `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-requires `encodedContext.length() == 6` and slices the grant shortcut as `substring(4, 6)`, which implicitly assumes the shortcut is exactly 2 chars. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` registers shortcuts without validating length or forbidding ':'; thus an extension providing a 1/3+ char shortcut (or one containing ':') will cause the server to mint access token IDs that its own decoder rejects via `IllegalArgumentException` on the length check. This mismatch is introduced/exposed by the diff and is verifiable in the added encoder/decoder logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut put() into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts unconditionally with no collision check, bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs. When a new grant implementation is later deployed (the exact scenario the refresh path exists for) and its shortcut collides with an existing one, the put silently overwrites the mapping and previously issued tokens carrying that shortcut decode to the wrong grant type; the size-equality guard that protects the startup path protects nothing here.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the “refresh maps” code paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() do unconditional put()s into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without any duplicate/collision validation. Unlike postInit(), these paths never re-check for duplicate shortcuts/IDs, so a newly deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with a colliding shortcut can silently overwrite an existing shortcut->grant mapping (grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)) while still adding a new grantType->shortcut entry (grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)), causing inconsistent mappings and potentially decoding tokens with that shortcut to the wrong grant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Encode and decode degrade asymmetrically: encode lazily learns unknown grants (or falls back to 'na' for null), but getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on any unknown session/token/grant shortcut rather than mapping it to UNKNOWN. During a rolling deploy where a new grant type (or a new shortcut) exists on some nodes but not others, or after a grant provider is removed, the nodes lacking the registration throw a hard error on token IDs their peers issued, instead of degrading to SessionType.UNKNOWN/TokenType.UNKNOWN the way the legacy no-colon path already does — turning a partial deployment into user-visible token-processing failures.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show asymmetric/tight decoding: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() returns UNKNOWN only for the legacy no-colon format, but for the new encoded format it throws IllegalArgumentException when a shortcut is not recognized (unknown session type/token type/grant type), e.g. `if (gt == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...) }`. Meanwhile encoding can fall back to `UNKNOWN`/"na" when the clientSessionContext grant type is null (getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext sets `grantType = UNKNOWN`). This makes cross-version/rolling-deploy tolerance worse for new token IDs, but the diff does not show any call sites where token processing/validation actually decodes token IDs and would therefore fail at runtime. So the compatibility concern is real and specific to the new logic, but the claimed user-visible token-processing failures are not directly verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The token-ID layout (2-char sessionType + 2-char tokenType + 2-char grant + ':' + uuid) is now hand-maintained in three places — the encoder's concatenation, the decoder's substring offsets, and this matcher — and the copies have already drifted (matcher uses substring(3,5) and a wrong comment about the '4th char'). The next change to the encoded format (adding a field, resizing a segment) must be applied in three independent sites across two modules; the drift that already happened here shows the pattern fails silently, and the next copy will again compile and pass while disagreeing with the encoder.

adjudication.rationale: The new test matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId()` is incorrect and has already drifted from the encoder/decoder format. The encoder builds a 6-char prefix (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) and the decoder reads grant via `substring(4, 6)`, but the matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` and also inverts the check (`if (...) return false;`), meaning it will almost always accept any `uuid` regardless of the expected grant shortcut. This is a real, diff-verifiable defect that causes silent misvalidation of token IDs in tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher inverts its grant-type check and reads the wrong substring: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` both indexes characters 3-4 (token-type tail + grant-type head) instead of the grant shortcut at characters 4-5, and returns false (mismatch) when they DO match. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All access-token jti values silently flip from UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' unconditionally in initToken, with no feature flag, realm option, or provider default that restores the legacy format (only the fallback decoder tolerates old IDs; there is no off switch for new issuance). Every external consumer and operator tooling that assumed the UUID jti format — an invariant the test suite itself encoded in isUUID() until this PR — starts seeing the new composite format on upgrade with no way to opt out short of deploying a different SPI provider; this format change to a publicly observable token field goes well beyond 'implement the framework' and should be an explicitly accepted decision, not a side effect of wiring the default encoder.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a deliberate, unconditional change to access token `jti`/ID generation in `TokenManager.initToken`: instead of `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (a UUID), it now always obtains `TokenContextEncoderProvider` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, producing a `6-char-context:rawId` format. The default provider is wired via the new internal SPI registration (`META-INF/services/...TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` and `org.keycloak.provider.Spi`), and there is no feature flag/realm option in this diff to retain legacy issuance. Tests were updated to stop asserting `isUUID()` and instead validate the new composite format, confirming the externally observable change. This is primarily a backwards-compatibility/operational impact concern rather than a verifiable correctness defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The unit test bypasses the factory's real wiring by hand-populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts in before(), so postInit registration, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation, and both lazy-refresh fallbacks in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory have zero coverage. A regression in the registry — e.g., the startup duplicate-shortcut check firing on the stock grant set, a lazy refresh writing a colliding shortcut over an existing mapping (the runtime put calls bypass the size-based validation entirely), or getShortcutByGrantType returning the wrong grant — ships unnoticed, while the tests that do exist only exercise a two-grant hand-built map.

adjudication.rationale: The new registry/validation logic lives in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() (building grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts from OAuth2GrantType factories and enforcing the duplicate-shortcut size check) and in the lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut(). In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the test bypasses this wiring by manually populating factory.grantsByShortcuts and factory.grantsToShortcuts and never calls postInit(), so the duplicate-shortcut validation and both lazy-refresh fallbacks are indeed untested by the added unit test and regressions there could ship without coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor's null-check for rawTokenId is a copy-paste error: it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time, so the documented 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' invariant is never enforced. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException (not an error signal distinguishable from a crash) for any client-influenced token-id string that contains a colon but has an invalid 6-char prefix or unknown shortcut, rather than degrading to the UNKNOWN/old-format handling used for colon-less ids. The new public provider API is explicitly intended for decoding token ids retrieved from tokens; any current or future call site that passes an untrusted token-id string (introspection/revocation token hints, event-detail lookups, stored session references) without try/catch turns malformed user input into an unhandled RuntimeException and an HTTP 500 on the endpoint, instead of the old-format fallback path the same method defines two branches earlier; the exception messages also echo the raw attacker-controlled string back into server logs/error handlers.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, only colon-less IDs fall back to UNKNOWN/old-format handling. If a caller passes an ID containing ':' but with an invalid 6-char context prefix (encodedContext.length() != 6) or unknown shortcuts, the method throws IllegalArgumentException and includes the attacker-controlled encodedTokenId in the exception message. The diff does not show any call site that feeds this method untrusted/user-supplied token-id strings without catching exceptions, so the claimed HTTP 500 impact is plausible but not verifiable from the PR itself; however, the mismatch in behavior (fallback vs hard-throw) is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher's grant-shortcut check is doubly broken (inverted condition plus wrong substring offset), so it can never fail on grant content and the matcher degenerates to a bare 'colon followed by UUID' check. Line 483 reads `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` — two independent bugs: (1) the condition returns false (mismatch) when the shortcut EQUALS the expected value, the inverse of the intent; (2) substring(3,5) extracts chars 3-4, which are the tokenType shortcut's 2nd char plus the grantType shortcut's 1st char (grant shortcut actually lives at indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, contradicting even the comment on line 482). Since tokenType shortcuts are 'rt'/'lt'/'un', substring(3,5) is always 't?' or 'n?', which never equals any registered shortcut ('ac','cc','rt','ci','dg','pg','pc','te','ro','na'), so the guard never fires and matchesSafely reduces to `items.length == 2 && isUUID().matches(items[1])`. Every integration test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore passes even if TokenManager.initToken encodes no grant type, the wrong grant type, or a garbage prefix — the entire purpose of switching these expectations from isUUID() to isAccessTokenId(shortcut) is unverified, giving false confidence that the new context-encoding wiring works end-to-end.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant-shortcut validation is incorrect in two ways visible in the diff: (1) it returns false when the extracted shortcut *equals* the expected value (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), which is inverted logic; (2) it extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` even though the encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType) as implemented in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), so the grant shortcut should be at indices 4-5 (i.e., substring(4,6)), not 3-4. As written, the matcher effectively ignores/does not correctly enforce the expected grant shortcut and largely devolves to checking `prefix:UUID` structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes vacuously via a NullPointerException from the uninitialized factory, not via the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' validation, and the broad catch(RuntimeException) guarantees any exception satisfies it. The @Before method (lines 33-44) never calls factory.postInit(), so factory.sessionFactory stays null and grantsByShortcuts contains only 'ro','cc','na'. getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678") resolves shortcut 'ac' via factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which finds nothing in the map and dereferences the null sessionFactory in its lazy-refresh path (`sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory), throwing NullPointerException — which the catch (RuntimeException iae) on line 76 swallows, so the test passes. The IllegalArgumentException('Unknown value ... for grant type') path the test name claims to verify is never reached; the test would equally pass on a StringIndexOutOfBounds or any other crash, and even after fixing the NPE, catch(RuntimeException) instead of IllegalArgumentException with a message assertion means the test still cannot distinguish the intended validation error from an unrelated failure.
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that `catch(RuntimeException)` is overly broad and allows the test to pass on unrelated exceptions, and recommends catching `IllegalArgumentException` (and even asserting the message). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only encoder path actually used in production (TokenManager.initToken) — nor the factory's postInit registration/duplicate-shortcut validation or lazy-refresh logic. However, the only new test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) exercises only getTokenContextFromTokenId(...) and encodeTokenId(...) using hand-built grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps; none of its tests call getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, so the sessionType derivation from clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE), the lightweight-token detection via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and the Constants.GRANT_TYPE -> "na" fallback are not covered. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' guard never runs. A null rawTokenId passes construction silently and encodeTokenId then produces a token ID with the literal suffix ':null', which later fails the 6-char-prefix decode check in getTokenContextFromTokenId and cannot be round-tripped; the intended fail-fast invariant (all four fields non-null) does not hold.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null check intended for `rawTokenId` is incorrectly written as `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so `rawTokenId` is never validated (diff: `AccessTokenContext.java` lines showing four requireNonNull calls with `grantType` duplicated). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy-map-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut write new grant/shortcut pairs into the maps with plain put() and no duplicate-shortcut validation, bypassing the size-equality check that postInit performs. When a new grant provider is registered after postInit and its getShortcut() collides with an existing grant's shortcut, the put() silently overwrites the existing mapping, so tokens already minted with that shortcut decode to the wrong grant type — a silent repurposing of an existing encoded value with no startup-time error to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() builds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and validates duplicates only once via the size-equality check. However, both lazy refresh paths can later mutate these maps with plain put(): getShortcutByGrantType() adds (shortcut->grantType, grantType->shortcut) when a new grantType is discovered, and getGrantTypeByShortcut() adds mappings when a new shortcut is discovered. Neither path re-validates uniqueness of shortcuts/IDs, so a newly deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with a colliding getShortcut() can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping in grantsByShortcuts, making previously minted token IDs decode to a different grant type without any error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are non-final, package-private mutable maps initialized only in postInit, with lookups reading them lazily afterwards. Any lookup (encodeTokenId or getShortcutByGrantType) invoked before postInit completes dereferences null and throws NPE, and the mutable package-visible state is a second initialization path (the new unit test already bypasses init/postInit and assigns the maps directly), so the next change that touches factory lifecycle risks an uninitialized-maps failure that startup validation will not catch.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are package-private, mutable, and only initialized in `postInit(...)` (they remain null after `init(...)`). Methods used by the provider (`getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) dereference these maps without null checks, so if `TokenContextEncoderProvider` is created/used before `postInit` runs, it would NPE. The new unit test demonstrates the maps can be bypass-initialized via direct assignment because of the package-private visibility, which increases lifecycle fragility. However, the diff alone does not prove the Keycloak SPI lifecycle will call `create()`/use the provider before `postInit`, so this is a concrete robustness/encapsulation issue rather than a verifiable runtime defect from the PR itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second call, intended to validate rawTokenId, re-checks grantType, so a null rawTokenId passes validation. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and flows into encodeTokenId, producing token jti values like 'onrtcc:null'; the fail-fast guard promised by the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' message never fires, and the misleading message blames grantType when debugging.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) (the tokenType's last char plus the grantType's first char) instead of substring(4, 6), AND inverts the match condition — 'if (equals(expected)) return false' — so the grant assertion can never fail for a wrong grant and would fail for the correct one. Every event assertion using this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) silently passes regardless of which grant type was encoded into the token ID; the matcher only checks '6-char prefix : UUID', so a regression encoding the wrong grant into token IDs ships undetected — the assertion reports verification success while verifying nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is encoded as the last 2 chars of the 6-char context prefix (sessionType 2 + tokenType 2 + grant 2) per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, so it should be extracted with substring(4, 6). The diff shows it uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which overlaps tokenType/grantType. Additionally, the matcher logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` causes the matcher to fail when the expected shortcut matches, and pass when it doesn't, meaning event assertions using this matcher will not correctly validate the encoded grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit validates shortcut uniqueness by map-size comparison but never validates that each grant shortcut is exactly 2 characters, while the getShortcut() javadoc in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory actively recommends '3-letters shortcut'. A grant factory (especially a custom one following the javadoc) returning a 1- or 3-char shortcut passes startup validation, but every token it produces gets a 5- or 7-char prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with 'Expected length of 6' — all tokens for that grant fail any future decode, and the misdocumented contract steers implementers into exactly that breakage.

The candidate goes further by explaining the concrete failure mode (token length/prefix decoding) and missing validation, but it still centers on the documentation being misleading relative to real usage/contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy re-registration branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut (commented 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed') are unreachable in practice because postInit already registers every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory at boot, and if they ever do execute they add mappings via ConcurrentHashMap.put without the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit enforces. Dead code that carries a correctness hazard: if any runtime path ever registers a grant factory after postInit, a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing grantsByShortcuts entry, so previously issued tokens decode as the wrong grant type with no error — the exact corruption the postInit check exists to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds lazy “Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed” branches in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut that mutate grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts via ConcurrentHashMap.put without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation performed in postInit. That is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness hazard (a newly discovered grant/shortcut collision could silently overwrite mappings and affect decoding). However, the finding’s claim that these branches are "unreachable in practice" cannot be verified from the diff alone (the code itself anticipates late deployment), and no concrete failing runtime path is shown here, so it’s better classified as an important design/edge-case issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws raw IllegalArgumentException on attacker-craftable jti content (wrong 6-char prefix length, or unknown session/token/grant shortcut) and no caller in this diff catches it. The jti of an access token is client-visible and client-controllable in crafted tokens; any future caller that invokes this method during token validation, introspection, or logout converts a crafted jti into an unhandled RuntimeException and a 500 response where an invalid-token 4xx belongs. No shipped path in this diff is affected yet, but the provider contract invites exactly that caller.

adjudication.rationale: In the added `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId`, malformed `encodedTokenId` values can trigger `IllegalArgumentException` (e.g., `encodedContext.length() != 6` or unknown session/token/grant shortcuts). The SPI interface exposes this method, but within this diff no production code calls `getTokenContextFromTokenId` (only tests do); current production usage in `TokenManager#initToken` only calls `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` and `encodeTokenId`. So it’s a concrete, diff-grounded contract/robustness concern for future callers rather than a verifiable defect in the shipped code paths shown here.
